key_facts: ‘Urticaria’ where **each wheal lasts > 24 h**, burns or hurts, and leaves **bruising or brown staining**.
**Immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis**; low C3 / C4 and anti-C1q in the hypocomplementaemic form.
Mark a wheal to time it; complement, ESR / CRP, urine, ANA; **refer for biopsy**; antihistamines help itch, not the vasculitis.
**HUVS** with lupus, kidney, lung (COPD-like) or eye involvement.

sections.title: Overview
blocks: **Urticarial vasculitis (UV):** a small-vessel (leukocytoclastic) vasculitis that presents as **urticaria-like lesions**. Two forms:

ul: **Normocomplementaemic UV** (~70–80%): usually skin-limited, often idiopathic, and milder.

**Hypocomplementaemic UV** (~20–30%): associated with systemic disease. Its severe form is **HUVS** (McDuffie syndrome; CHCC 2012: **anti-C1q vasculitis**), with **arthritis, angioedema, ocular inflammation, COPD, glomerulonephritis** and a strong overlap with **SLE**.

sections.title: Pathophysiology and pathology
blocks: Immune-complex deposition in post-capillary venules with complement consumption (low C3/C4/C1q). **Anti-C1q autoantibodies** in HUVS. **Causes**:

ul: **drugs** (ACE-i, penicillins, sulfonamides, fluoxetine, cimetidine, diltiazem, thiazides, potassium iodide, NSAIDs, glatiramer; also TNF inhibitors)
**paraproteins** (IgM — **Schnitzler syndrome** — and IgA gammopathy), mixed cryoglobulinaemia

Urticarial vasculitis
Ordinary (chronic spontaneous) urticaria
rows: Fever, arthralgia, abdominal pain, angioedema, lymphadenopathy, eye/kidney/lung involvement (especially HUVS)
**LCV** (fibrinoid necrosis, nuclear dust, RBC extravasation); DIF Ig/C3 around vessels ± lupus band at the DEJ
Dermal oedema, sparse infiltrate, no vasculitis

fig.caption: Circle a wheal with a pen and photograph it daily. An ordinary wheal is gone within 24 hours; urticarial vasculitis persists for days and leaves a bruise-like stain.
fig.alt: Three days of a pen-circled wheal ending as a bruise

ul: **Biopsy a lesion** (H&E + DIF, ideally a lesion <48 h old) — essential, because the clinical overlap with urticaria is large.

**Underlying cause and organ screen**: **C3, C4, C1q, anti-C1q, CH50**; **ANA, dsDNA, ENA (Ro/La/Sm)**; ESR/CRP, FBC, U&E/eGFR, LFT; **urinalysis + uPCR** (± renal biopsy); **hepatitis B/C**, HIV, EBV; **SPEP/immunofixation** (IgM paraprotein — Schnitzler), **cryoglobulins**; ASO; CXR and **PFTs** (COPD/emphysema in HUVS, especially smokers); **ophthalmology** (uveitis/episcleritis/conjunctivitis); a cancer screen if indicated

**HUVS criteria (Schwartz 1982):** **Major (both required):** chronic urticarial exanthem for **≥6 months**, and **hypocomplementaemia**; **Minor (≥2):** dermal venulitis on biopsy; arthralgia/arthritis; uveitis/episcleritis; glomerulonephritis; recurrent abdominal pain; positive C1q precipitin (anti-C1q); **Exclusions:** cryoglobulinaemia, high-titre anti-dsDNA, HBV, C1-INH deficiency

sections.title: Differential diagnoses

ddx.name: Chronic spontaneous urticaria
ddx.f: Wheals < 24 h, itch, normal skin after, antihistamine-responsive.

ddx.name: SLE
ddx.f: Photosensitivity, ANA +, low complement, nephritis; ~50% of HUVS meet SLE criteria.

blocks: Chronic spontaneous urticaria; **SLE** (photosensitivity, ANA+, low complement and nephritis also fit — HUVS and SLE overlap, and ~50% of HUVS patients meet SLE criteria); Schnitzler syndrome (IgM paraprotein, fever, bone pain); cryoglobulinaemic vasculitis; serum-sickness-like reaction; Still's disease; neutrophilic urticarial dermatosis; urticarial bullous pemphigoid; erythema multiforme.

sections.title: Management

ul: **Refer** to dermatology ± rheumatology/renal (urgently if renal involvement — the case has a creatinine of ~203 µmol/L).
Stop any suspect drug (ACE-i, NSAIDs, etc.). Yellow Card.
**Symptomatic:** non-sedating antihistamines (help itch/angioedema, but not the vasculitis), NSAIDs only if renal function allows.

**Specialist ladder:** **dapsone**, **colchicine**, **hydroxychloroquine** (first-line for mild/normocomplementaemic disease) → oral corticosteroids for flares → steroid-sparing **mycophenolate, azathioprine, methotrexate** → **rituximab** (HUVS/SLE), omalizumab (case reports, normocomplementaemic UV), anakinra/canakinumab (Schnitzler). Cyclophosphamide/MMF for nephritis.
**Shared-care monitoring** (dapsone — FBC, LFT, methaemoglobin; HCQ — annual eye screening after 5 years, or from 1 year if risk factors, RCOphth 2020; MMF — FBC/LFT; contraception).

blocks: Recognition (do not keep up-titrating antihistamines for "urticaria" that bruises), urinalysis, bloods, drug review, referral, and shared-care monitoring.

refer.t: Wheals with **joint pain, fever, abdominal pain, breathlessness or abnormal urine**: suspected systemic (hypocomplementaemic) disease.
Wheals > 24 h, burning or bruising: dermatology for biopsy.

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: Wheals with joint pain, fever, abdominal pain, breathlessness or abnormal urine: suspect **systemic (hypocomplementaemic) disease**, refer urgently.

blocks: Wheals lasting >24 h, painful, leaving bruising; systemic symptoms; abnormal urine, creatinine or complement; angioedema with laryngeal symptoms (999); eye pain/redness (same-day ophthalmology); breathlessness.

pearls: "**Wheals that last more than a day, burn, and leave a bruise = biopsy.**"
Ask patients to **circle a wheal with a pen** and photograph it daily — it documents duration (cheap, effective).

quiz.a: Complement: low C3, C4, C1q; anti-C1q.
